newsitem.title: GERMANY: Grundig CEO resigns with immediate effect.
newsitem.headline: Grundig CEO resigns with immediate effect.

text.p: Troubled German home electronics maker Grundig AG said on Monday former CEO Pieter van der Wal quit, leaving his office six weeks sooner than expected.

"I had told the company I was willing to remain in service for two months. But today I must recognise that the basis for the association has fallen away," van der Wal wrote in a letter to supervisory board chief Christian Schwarz-Schilling.

Grundig said it had not yet found a successor, although last week it hired two consulting firms to help find a new chief executive and a business partner willing to invest in production sites in Germany.

Van der Wal resigned on January 20 under heavy employee protests against his plan to turn around the loss-making stereo and television company by laying off a third of its 8,500 employees. He planned to sell off non-core operations and move TV production out of Germany to Austria.

His ouster followed the departure of Dutch giant Philips Electronics NV, which ran Grundig until January 1. Grundig lost an estimated 350 million marks ($213 million) in 1996, after a 600 million mark loss in 1995.
